speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; how many hours of life has it been since you were born, and is your vomiting forceful or projectile?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus. The combination of bilious vomiting in a newborn at six hours of life is an immediate surgical emergency, and the history of a sibling with pyloric stenosis does not explain this acute presentation. Please prepare the patient for an emergent Upper GI series to confirm the diagnosis.
